LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsIndependent: The coordinates of a pair with joint law p are independent if p is the product of its first and second marginal laws.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsIndependentOf: Under a source law p, X and Y are independent if the joint law of (X,Y) equals the product of the marginal laws of X and Y.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsCondIndependent: For a joint probability mass function of (X,Y,Z), conditional independence of X and Y given Z means that Pr[X=a,Y=b,Z=c] Pr[Z=c] = Pr[X=a,Z=c] Pr[Y=b,Z=c] for every a,b,c. Both sides are zero when Pr[Z=c] = 0.

Let X,Y,Z be functions of a source with probability mass function p. X and Y are conditionally independent given Z when their induced joint masses satisfy Pr[X=a,Y=b,Z=c] Pr[Z=c] = Pr[X=a,Z=c] Pr[Y=b,Z=c] for every a,b,c.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isCondIndependent: A triple law has its first two coordinates conditionally independent given the third exactly when the same condition holds after exchanging the first two coordinates.
For variables on a common source, Y is independent of X given Z exactly when X is independent of Y given Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependent_iff: Let p be the joint probability mass function of (X,Y). The coordinates are independent exactly when p(a,b) = Pr[X=a] Pr[Y=b] for every pair of values a,b.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependent_ind: If a pair has the product law p ⊗ q, its coordinates are independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependent_map: The two coordinates of a pair are independent after swapping their order exactly when they were independent before the swap.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependentOf_i: For any X,Y on a source with law p, independence is equivalent to equality of their induced joint law with the product of the two separately induced marginal laws.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependentOf_c: Let X and Y be functions of a source with probability mass function p. If X and Y are independent under p, then X and f(Y) are independent under p for every function f on the values of Y.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependentOf_i: For measurable random variables X,Y with measurable singletons in their value spaces, independence defined by factorization of the induced probability mass functions is equivalent to independence as measurable functions under the measure of the source law.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isIndependentOf_s: For variables X,Y on a common source, Y and X are independent exactly when X and Y are independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_eq_zer: For a finite pair law p, I(X;Y) = 0 exactly when p is the product of its marginals.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfoOf_eq_z: For finite-valued variables X and Y on a common source, I(X;Y) = 0 exactly when X and Y are independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_eq_en: For a finite pair law, H(X|Y) = H(X) exactly when the joint distribution factors into its marginals.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_eq_: For finite-valued variables X,Y, conditioning on Y preserves the entropy of X exactly when X and Y are independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropy_eq_a: For a finite pair law p, H(X,Y) = H(X)+H(Y) exactly when p is the product of its marginals.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_eq: For two finite-valued variables on the same source, H(X,Y) = H(X)+H(Y) exactly when X and Y are independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropy_addi: For a finite joint law, additivity of joint entropy H(X,Y) = H(X)+H(Y) characterizes independence of its coordinates.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.jointEntropyOf_ad: For finite-valued variables on a common source, joint entropy is the sum of their individual entropies exactly when the variables are independent.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq: For a finite triple law, I(X;Y|Z) is zero exactly when I(X;Y|Z=c) is zero for every c with Pr[Z=c] > 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isCondIndependent: Let (X,Y,Z) have a joint probability mass function, with X and Y finite-valued. X and Y are conditionally independent given Z exactly when they are independent under the conditional joint law at every c with Pr[Z=c] > 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq: For a finite triple law, I(X;Y|Z) = 0 exactly when its first two coordinates are conditionally independent given the third.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfoOf_: For finite-valued variables X,Y,Z on a common source, I(X;Y|Z) = 0 exactly when X and Y are conditionally independent given Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_eq_co: For a finite triple law, H(X|Y,Z) = H(X|Z) exactly when its first two coordinates are conditionally independent given the third.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_eq_: For finite-valued variables X,Y,Z on a common source, H(X|Y,Z) = H(X|Z) exactly when X and Y are conditionally independent given Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_pair_: For a finite triple law, H(X,Y|Z) = H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z) exactly when its first two coordinates are conditionally independent given its third.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_pai: For three finite-valued variables on a common source, the identity H(X,Y|Z) = H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z) holds exactly when X and Y are conditionally independent given Z.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_pair_: In a finite triple law, conditional independence of X and Y given Z is equivalent to additivity of conditional joint entropy, H(X,Y|Z) = H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropyOf_pai: For finite-valued variables on a common source, conditional joint entropy is additive, H(X,Y|Z) = H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z), exactly when X and Y are conditionally independent given Z.
